divergence.reason: TypeScript 6 keeps the alias identity of `React.Ref<T>` on its resolved union, so the pinned oracle reports one opaque external reference `React.Ref<HTMLInputElement>` beside `undefined`; TypeScript 7 hands the resolver the expanded union instead, so the members report individually (`React.RefObject<T | null>` with its substituted argument, `React.RefCallback`, and folded `null`) and the optional property widens to four members. Inside the expanded members the TypeScript 7 substitution view also names the DOM element through React's augmented namespace chain (`HTMLInputElement` with namespaces ['React']) where TypeScript 6 reported the bare global name. The ownership policy itself behaves identically in both compilers - every dependency-owned arm summarizes as a named external reference rather than expanding signatures - so all remaining differences sit in the compiler's union identity view, and every non-alias prop of this fixture reproduces the upstream oracle byte-for-byte.
